This market will resolve to the individual who de facto holds and exercises the powers of the head of state of the Islamic Republic of Iran on December 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, “de facto holds” refers to the individual who exercises primary governing authority over the Iranian state at that time, including effective control over the armed forces, national institutions, and core executive decision-making, regardless of formal title, constitutional designation, or international recognition.

Formal appointment, recognition by the United Nations, or recognition by foreign governments is not required.

If more than one individual claims to be head of state, this market will resolve to the individual who demonstrably exercises primary governing control within Iran’s territory at the specified time.

Indicators of de facto authority may include control over the armed forces and security services; control over executive ministries and state administrative institutions; enforcement of national laws; issuance of binding national directives; and effective control over the capital and core state infrastructure.

Symbolic status, foreign recognition without domestic control, nomination without effective authority, or expired prior service will not qualify.

If no individual exercises effective governing control at the specified time, this market will resolve to “No Head of State”.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting assessing who exercises effective governing authority at the specified time.

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, flight suspensions, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Israel will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israeli aviation authorities; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

edge_board.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the September 2026 meeting?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

edge_board.description: US-Iran tensions remain elevated following the April 2026 two-week ceasefire, the June memorandum of understanding setting a 60-day framework for addressing the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions relief, and Iran's nuclear program, and subsequent July violations that included Iranian strikes on commercial vessels and US retaliatory actions. President Trump declared the truce effectively over amid these exchanges, while the US revoked related sanctions waivers; both sides have since signaled willingness to avoid full-scale resumption but continue limited strikes and naval pressures. Negotiations involving Pakistan and other mediators focus on deconfliction mechanisms in Lebanon and freedom of navigation, with any new pause likely hinging on verifiable Iranian compliance and progress toward a final accord. Trader assessments reflect uncertainty over whether recent brinkmanship will yield another structured pause or escalate before scheduled diplomatic deadlines.
edge_board.question: US x Iran Effective Ceasefire by August 14?

edge_board.description: Traders assign a 96% probability that China will not invade Taiwan by December 31, 2026, reflecting the absence of large-scale amphibious mobilization, logistical buildup, or other indicators of imminent cross-strait assault in the five months remaining. U.S. intelligence assessments, including the ODNI’s March 2026 threat report, conclude that Chinese leaders lack a fixed timeline and favor sustained coercion short of war through air defense identification zone incursions, coast guard patrols, and exercises simulating blockades rather than island landings. Recent months have shown normalized but reduced military activity around Taiwan alongside diplomatic focus on the 2028 Taiwanese elections. Realistic shifts could still arise from rapid escalation following a major miscalculation, abrupt policy reversal, or unforeseen regional crisis, though current patterns indicate continued gray-zone pressure instead.
edge_board.question: Will China invade Taiwan by end of 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of the Republic of China (Taiwan) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Territory under the administration of the Republic of China including any inhabited islands will qualify, however uninhabited islands will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by China, Taiwan, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

edge_board.description: Corporate announcement
edge_board.question: Will any company announce that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) before Oct 1, 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria: If any company (public or private) officially announces that it has achieved Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) after market issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes. To qualify, the announcement must explicitly state that the company has achieved, attained, reached, or developed Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), or that it has achieved, attained, reached, or developed “AGI.” Statements that describe “AGI-like,” “AGI-level,” “near-AGI,” or “toward AGI” systems without explicitly stating that the company has achieved/attained/reached/developed AGI do not qualify. For purposes of this market, a “company” includes any publicly traded company or any privately held company whose existence and corporate identity is verifiable and whose financing/valuation or corporate profile is covered by at least two of the listed major business news sources.

edge_board.description: Freddie Mac
edge_board.question: When will Freddie Mac officially announce an IPO?
edge_board.resolution_criteria: If Freddie Mac confirms an IPO before Aug 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes. An IPO is confirmed if 1) the SEC declares the company's Form S-1 effective OR 2) the IPO is priced OR 3) a securities exchange has assigned a ticker to it. As long as any of those events occur, the market will immediately resolve to Yes, even if the company does not start trading until after Aug 1, 2026.
